text: Lighting forms the foundation of photography, a practice defined by freezing time through controlled illumination. The quality of any image depends entirely on this element; insufficient or poor lighting diminishes the result, whereas adequate sources ensure brightness and clarity. Sharpness requires stability, making a tripod indispensable for holding the camera steady during exposure. To achieve even and gentle illumination, photographers often employ softboxes or light bags, which diffuse harsh rays and produce more flattering portraits than direct light alone.
